commit-message|deepseek|base.text:
perf(cache): skip relink in LRU get() when entry is already head

Profiling showed get() taking 11% of request time on the session store
hot path, almost all of it unconditional unlink/relink of entries that
were already at the front of the list. Only move the entry when it is
not already the head.

Adds a test asserting 1,000 repeated hits on the head entry perform
zero list mutations. No behavior change intended.

pr-description|deepseek|base.text:
## Summary

The invoice export job now streams rows to the CSV writer in batches of 500 instead of loading the entire result set into memory.

## Motivation

The previous implementation held the full result set in memory. A 400,000-row export peaked at roughly 2.1 GB and was OOM-killed twice last month on the 2 GB worker.

## Impact

- Peak memory for a local run of the same 400,000 rows dropped from ~2.1 GB to ~180 MB.
- Wall-clock time increased from 41 s to 47 s.
- CSV output is byte-identical to before, verified with a diff on a 10,000-row fixture.

## Implementation notes

- Batch size is controlled by the `EXPORT_BATCH_ROWS` constant in `jobs/export/config.ts`.

## Not included

- The payments export has the same pattern and is left for a follow-up.

## Rollout

No feature flag and no migration required.

code-review-comment|deepseek|base.text:
This retry loop can double-charge the customer. `gateway.charge` isn't idempotent and takes no idempotency key, but `GatewayError` is also raised on timeouts — i.e. after the gateway may have already captured the funds. In that case we `continue` to the next card (or raise `PaymentFailed`), and the caller retries `charge`, charging the customer again.

We need to distinguish "definitely not charged" from "unknown/possibly charged" before retrying. Options:
- Pass an idempotency key through to the gateway so retries are safe (requires gateway support).
- On timeout/ambiguous errors, stop and surface a distinct state (e.g. `PaymentUnknown`) instead of `PaymentFailed`, so the caller reconciles rather than blindly retrying.
- Only retry on errors that guarantee no capture occurred.

As written, this is unsafe to merge.

code-review-comment|deepseek|smd.text:
This retries across cards on any `GatewayError`, but a timeout means the charge may already have captured. The caller then retries `charge` on `PaymentFailed`, so a timeout on card 1 can charge card 1, fall through to card 2, charge that too, and the caller's retry can charge again — the customer is billed multiple times for one order.

`gateway.charge` takes no idempotency key, so there's no way to make the retry safe at this layer. Two options:

1. Add an idempotency key to `gateway.charge` (keyed on `order.id`) and pass it through, so a retry of the same order is a no-op at the gateway. This is the fix if the gateway supports it.
2. If it doesn't, don't retry on timeout. Distinguish the error: a connection-refused or pre-send failure is safe to try the next card; a timeout is not — surface it as an unknown state and reconcile against the gateway before retrying.

Also worth confirming: is falling through to the next card on *any* `GatewayError` intended? A decline on card 1 and a timeout on card 1 need different handling, and right now they're treated the same.

docstring|deepseek|base.text:
"""Merge overlapping or adjacent intervals.

Args:
    intervals: An iterable of (start, end) tuples representing intervals.
        The intervals may be provided in any order.
    gap: A non-negative numeric tolerance specifying the maximum allowed
        distance between two intervals for them to be merged. Two intervals
        are merged when the start of the next interval is less than or equal
        to the end of the previous interval plus ``gap``. Defaults to 0,
        which merges only overlapping or touching intervals.

Returns:
    A list of (start, end) tuples representing the merged intervals, sorted
    in ascending order by start. Returns an empty list if ``intervals`` is
    empty.

Examples:
    >>> merge_intervals([(1, 3), (2, 6), (8, 10), (15, 18)])
    [(1, 6), (8, 10), (15, 18)]
    >>> merge_intervals([(1, 2), (4, 5)], gap=2)
    [(1, 5)]
"""

docstring|deepseek|smd.text:
```python
"""Merge overlapping or adjacent intervals into a minimal set.

Sorts the input by start, then coalesces each interval into the previous
one when its start is within ``gap`` of the previous end. The result is
sorted by start and contains no two intervals closer than ``gap``.

Args:
    intervals: Iterable of ``(start, end)`` pairs. Each pair is unpacked
        as exactly two values, so longer sequences raise ``ValueError``.
        Ordering must be defined for the start values (they are compared
        during the sort). The input is not mutated.
    gap: Maximum distance between one interval's end and the next
        interval's start for them to be merged. ``0`` merges only
        overlapping or touching intervals; a positive value also merges
        intervals separated by up to ``gap``. Negative values are not
        rejected and will leave some overlapping intervals unmerged.

Returns:
    A new list of ``(start, end)`` tuples, sorted by start, with no two
    intervals within ``gap`` of each other. Empty if ``intervals`` is
    empty.

Raises:
    TypeError: If an element is not iterable or its start/end cannot be
        compared or added to ``gap``.
    ValueError: If an element does not unpack into exactly two values.
"""
```

code-review-comment|sonnet|base.text:
**Risk of double charging:** a `GatewayError` can be raised on a timeout after the gateway has already captured the funds, and this code treats it the same as a clean decline. It moves on and charges the next card, so the customer can be charged twice in a single call. Since `gateway.charge` isn't idempotent, there's no way to detect that the first charge went through.

It gets worse at the caller. On `PaymentFailed` the caller retries `charge`, which starts over at the first card. If funds were captured on any attempt, every retry can capture them again, and the customer ends up with several charges for one order.

Suggestions:

- Don't treat all `GatewayError`s as "safe to try the next card." Separate definite declines (card rejected, insufficient funds), which are safe to fall through on, from ambiguous failures (timeouts, connection errors, 5xx), which should stop the loop and surface as an "unknown outcome" state.
- For the ambiguous case, reconcile before any retry. Look up the charge by order ID on the gateway side, or record a pending payment attempt for the order and check it first.
- If the gateway offers an idempotency key (or a client-supplied reference we can query by), pass a stable per-order and per-card key. If it doesn't, we need our own persisted attempt record to get the same guarantee.
- The caller shouldn't blindly retry on `PaymentFailed`. Either use a distinct exception for "outcome unknown" that isn't retried, or make retries go through the reconciliation step above.

I'd also add a test where the first card raises a timeout-style `GatewayError` after capturing, and assert that no second charge is attempted.

code-review-comment|sonnet|smd.text:
Double-charge risk. A `GatewayError` on timeout can mean the gateway already captured funds, but the `except` treats every `GatewayError` as "not charged" and moves on to the next card. The customer can be charged on card 1 and again on card 2. Then the caller retries on `PaymentFailed`, which can charge every card again.

Since `gateway.charge` has no idempotency key, a failed call is only safe to retry if the error proves nothing was captured. Options:

1. Split `GatewayError` into definite declines (card declined, validation error: safe to try the next card) and ambiguous failures (timeout, connection reset: stop). For the ambiguous case, raise a distinct exception such as `PaymentUnknown(order.id)`, not `PaymentFailed`, so the caller doesn't retry.
2. Before any retry or fallback after an ambiguous error, look up the order's charges at the gateway (if it supports lookup by order reference) and reconcile.
3. Longer term, use a gateway or API version that accepts idempotency keys, and derive the key from `order.id` plus the card.

The caller must also stop retrying on the ambiguous path. A regression test should mock a timeout on card 1 and assert that card 2 is never charged and that `PaymentFailed` is not raised.

```python
"""Merge overlapping or nearby intervals into a minimal set of intervals.

Intervals are sorted by start value and combined whenever the next
interval begins at or before the end of the current merged interval plus
`gap`. The input is not modified.

Args:
    intervals: An iterable of (start, end) pairs of comparable, numeric
        values. Each pair is assumed to satisfy start <= end. The input
        does not need to be sorted.
    gap: The maximum distance between one interval's end and the next
        interval's start for the two to still be merged. With the default
        of 0, intervals merge only if they overlap or touch. Must be
        non-negative to behave sensibly.

Returns:
    A list of (start, end) tuples, sorted by start, with no two intervals
    overlapping or separated by `gap` or less. Returns an empty list if
    `intervals` is empty.

Examples:
    >>> merge_intervals([(1, 3), (2, 6), (8, 10)])
    [(1, 6), (8, 10)]
    >>> merge_intervals([(1, 2), (4, 5)], gap=2)
    [(1, 5)]
"""
```

```python
"""Merge overlapping or nearby intervals.

Intervals are sorted by start, then combined whenever the next start is
at most `gap` past the end of the current merged interval. Touching
intervals (start == previous end) always merge, even when `gap` is 0.

Args:
    intervals: Iterable of (start, end) pairs of mutually comparable
        numbers. Each must unpack to exactly two values and is assumed
        to satisfy start <= end; this is not validated. The input is
        not modified.
    gap: Maximum distance between one interval's end and the next
        interval's start for the two to still merge. Must support
        addition with the interval ends. Defaults to 0. A negative
        value requires intervals to overlap by at least abs(gap)
        before they merge.

Returns:
    A list of (start, end) tuples, sorted by start, with no two
    intervals mergeable under `gap`. Empty if `intervals` is empty.

Raises:
    TypeError: If values cannot be compared or added to `gap`.
    ValueError: If an element does not unpack to exactly two values.
"""
```

readme-intro|deepseek|smd.text:
# tidyfeed

Parse RSS 2.0 and Atom 1.0 into one normalized object shape. `parseFeed(xmlString)` returns `{ title, link, items }`, where each item is `{ id, title, link, published, summary }` and `published` is an ISO 8601 string or `null`. No dependencies, no network access: you supply the XML, tidyfeed parses it. The whole document is held in memory, so it is not suitable for feeds large enough to matter as a stream.

## Install

```sh
npm install tidyfeed
```

Requires Node 18 or later.

## Usage

```js
const { parseFeed } = require('tidyfeed');

const feed = parseFeed(xmlString);

feed.title;              // 'Example Blog'
feed.link;               // 'https://example.com/'
feed.items[0].id;        // stable id from guid or Atom id
feed.items[0].published; // '2024-03-01T12:00:00Z' or null
```

ESM: `import { parseFeed } from 'tidyfeed';`

## Not supported

RSS enclosures and media extensions are ignored. tidyfeed does not fetch feeds over the network.

## License

MIT

incident-summary|sonnet|smd.text:
**Resolved: Checkout errors after api v3.18 deploy**

Between 14:09 and 14:31 UTC, checkout was failing for most customers. Checkout error rate rose from 0.2% to 31% and returned below 1% at 14:31. Checkout was fully recovered by 14:34. Roughly 9,300 checkout attempts failed during this window.

**Customer impact:** No customer was double-charged. Failed attempts were not retried automatically, so affected customers need to place their order again.

**Open question:** We have not yet determined why staging did not catch the migration. A review is scheduled for Tuesday, and we will post findings afterward.
